title: Dynamic Typing and Truthiness Traps on Security Checks
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x; assert removal occurs whenever the interpreter runs with -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE set
security_mechanism: Python semantics silently weaken several guard idioms. assert is a statement the compiler deletes under -O, so a permission check written as assert disappears entirely in optimized deployments. Truthiness coerces None, 0, '', [] and {} to False, so 'if not user' style checks conflate 'absent' with 'present but empty' and can pass or fail authorization depending on payload shape. == calls __eq__, which attacker-influenced objects can override; a mutable default argument (def check(acl=[])) shares one object across calls, letting an earlier request's state satisfy a later request's check.

source_sink_clues.source: Deserialized request objects, JSON bodies whose field types the server does not pin (string vs array vs null), and values crossing call boundaries via mutable default arguments.
source_sink_clues.sink: assert used as an authorization/authentication gate; if/while truthiness checks over untrusted collections or IDs on security paths; mutable default arguments holding security state

tracking_guards: Check that authorization outcomes are enforced with explicit comparisons (is None, isinstance, ==/is against an exact expected value) and raised as exceptions rather than assert; check that JSON fields are type-validated before truthiness tests; check default arguments use None sentinels.
not_candidate_when: assert guards only internal invariants unreachable from input and deployment never runs with -O, the truthiness check is on a value provably non-empty by construction, or defaults are immutable/None-sentinel and state is per-call.
